I'll pull your intents and run the spending analysis to see what's idle.
## Short answer

**Yes — 0.80 USDC is genuinely stranded and recoverable right now.** That's the only real "dead" money. But there's a bigger, less obvious issue: you've authorized **67 USDC** of spending power against just **1.28 USDC** of actual spend.

## The idle money

| Intent | Purpose | State | Funded | Spent | Unspent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0xe88b…df16` | Marketing tools trial | **Revoked** | 1.00 | 0.20 | **0.80 ← stranded** |
| `0x5682…2f5b` | General ops discretionary | Active | 0.30 | 0.00 | 0.30 |
| `0xb530…7ca7` | Research subscriptions | Active | 0.40 | 0.10 | 0.30 |
| `0x4e08…bcf4` | Cloud infra autopay | Active | 1.20 | 0.98 | 0.22 |

1.62 USDC total sits funded-but-unspent, but only the 0.80 on the revoked intent is truly dead — that intent can never spend again ("Trial ended, tool not adopted"). The other 0.82 is live working capital behind active mandates.

## What to do

1. **Withdraw the remainder from `0xe88b…df16`** — now. No downside, no mandate to change. Recovers 0.80 USDC.
2. **Fix or kill `0x5682…2f5b`** — now. This one has a 10 USDC cap, a 2 USDC per-tx cap, **an empty merchant allowlist** (it can pay *any* address), and zero payments ever. It's your biggest containment hole. Either name the merchants it's meant to pay, or revoke it and pull the 0.30 back.
3. **Cut the cap on `0xb530…7ca7`** — this week. 50 USDC authorized, 0.10 spent. Per-tx cap of 5 USDC has never exceeded 2% usage. Merchant is allowlisted so blast radius is contained; this is just shrinking a pointless standing authorization.
4. **Raise the per-tx cap on `0x4e08…bcf4`** — this week. Opposite problem: both payments hit **98%** of the 0.50 cap to the same merchant. Your GPU/storage invoices are likely being clipped or split. It's also burned 49% of its total cap in two txs with 30 days left — at that rate it runs dry in about a week.

## Two caveats

**On items 2 and 3, the tool reports "recovers 10 USDC" and "recovers 49.9 USDC."** That's not cash coming back — those are *authorization* reductions. The actual money you can move to your wallet today is **0.80 USDC**, plus 0.30 more if you revoke the ops intent.

**"For a while" doesn't match the data.** Every payment across all four intents landed within a 90-second span on 2026-09-13. The 90-day analysis window has no real time series in it, so the "weekly cadence" read on the cloud intent and any spend-rate projections are inferred from the metadata string, not observed. If you expected months of history, something's wrong with the indexing — worth checking before you act on the cap changes.

Also worth noting: the `agent` address on all four intents is identical to your own payer address. That's either a test setup or a misconfiguration — no third-party agent is actually named in any of these mandates.

findings.title: 0.80 USDC idle on a revoked intent, recoverable immediately
findings.detail: 0xe88b…df16 (Marketing tools trial - Q3) is in Revoked state with 1.00 USDC funded and only 0.20 USDC spent across a single payment. The remaining 0.80 USDC is stranded — the intent can never spend it again, and the stated revoke reason ('Trial ended, tool not adopted') confirms no further use is expected. This is the only true idle capital in the set.

findings.title: Committed-but-unspent funding totals 1.62 USDC across all four intents
findings.detail: Funded balances that have not been spent: 0.80 (0xe88b…df16, revoked), 0.30 (0x5682…2f5b, active, zero payments), 0.30 (0xb530…7ca7, active), 0.22 (0x4e08…bcf4, active). Only the 0.80 on the revoked intent is recoverable without changing an active mandate; the other 0.82 is live working capital, though 0.30 of it sits behind an intent that has never transacted.

findings.title: 50 USDC cap against 0.10 USDC of spend on the research intent
findings.detail: 0xb530…7ca7 authorises 50 USDC total with a 5 USDC per-tx cap but has made one payment of 0.10 USDC (2% of perTxCap, 0.2% of totalCap). The allowlist is restricted to one merchant, which contains blast radius, but the headroom is ~500x observed spend and serves no demonstrated purpose.

findings.title: 10 USDC discretionary intent is unrestricted and has never paid anyone
findings.detail: 0x5682…2f5b carries a 10 USDC cap and a 2 USDC per-tx cap with merchantAllowlistSize=0 and unrestrictedMerchants=true. It has zero payments and zero spend, yet 0.30 USDC is funded and the mandate can pay any address up to its cap. An unbounded allowlist on the second-largest cap in the set with no usage history is the largest containment exposure here, not the largest dollar exposure.

findings.title: Cloud infra autopay is pinned at 98% of per-tx cap and will exhaust its total cap
findings.detail: Both payments on 0x4e08…bcf4 were 0.49 USDC against a 0.50 USDC per-tx cap (98%), to the same merchant 0x1111…1111. This is the signature of a throttled agent: the merchant's actual invoice may exceed the cap and is being clipped or split. It has also burned 49% of its 2 USDC total cap in two transactions with 30 days remaining on a stated weekly cadence — at ~0.98 USDC/week the cap is exhausted in roughly one more week, and funded balance (1.2 USDC) leaves only 0.22 USDC of runway.

actions.rationale: Intent is already Revoked with the tool not adopted; the 0.80 USDC funded remainder can never be spent and should be pulled back to the payer. No downside, no mandate change required.

A 10 USDC cap with an empty allowlist and zero payment history means any address can be paid up to 2 USDC per tx. Populate the allowlist with the merchants this agent is actually meant to pay; if none can be named, revoke instead and recover the 0.30 USDC funded.

50 USDC authorised against 0.10 USDC spent (0.2% used). Cut the total cap to a level anchored on observed subscription spend and reduce perTxCap from 5 USDC, which has never been approached (max 2% used). The allowlist is already restricted, so this is about shrinking the standing authorisation, not blast radius.

Two consecutive payments at 98% of the 0.50 USDC per-tx cap to a single known merchant indicate the cap is mis-sized against actual GPU/storage invoices. Raise perTxCap to clear the true invoice amount, and pair it with a total-cap or funding top-up review: at 0.98 USDC per week the 2 USDC total cap and 0.22 USDC unspent funding run out well before the 30 days remaining.

dataGaps: All four payments and all daily spend rows fall on a single day (2026-09-13), so the '90-day window' contains no real time series — spend rates, weekly cadence, and idle-day figures cannot be validated (idleDays=0 everywhere).
The true invoice amount from merchant 0x1111…1111 is unknown, so it cannot be confirmed whether the 0.49 USDC payments are clipped invoices, split payments, or genuinely sized transactions.
Merchant addresses have no names or categories, so 'restrict_merchants' on 0x5682…2f5b cannot be pre-populated from this data.

No information on why fundedUsdc is far below totalCapUsdc on every intent (e.g. 0.4 funded vs 50 cap on 0xb530…7ca7) — unclear whether funding is drip-fed by design, which changes how urgent cap reductions are.
No gas/fee data for withdrawRemainder, so net recovery on the 0.80 USDC idle balance is unverified.
